newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Getronics first half net jumps 45 percent.
newsitem.headline: Getronics first half net jumps 45 percent.

text.p: Dutch computer networks and engineering firm Getronics reported on Thursday a 45 percent rise in earnings for the first half of 1997, saying it expects further strong growth in net sales and profits for the rest of the year.

Net profits in the first half jumped to 79 million guilders ($38.3 million) from 54.5 million in the same period of 1996. Turnover increased by 19 percent to 1.28 billion guilders, while operating profits grew 18 percent to 107.8 million.
The increase in operating profit was generated by organic growth, and Getronics said business conditions in the second half would remain favourable.
"The earlier published expectation of a continuing strong growth in net sales and earnings is therefore maintained," the company said in a statement.
The strong rise in earnings was partially attributable to good performance from the group's RAET software unit, it added. Getronics acquired the outstanding 50 percent of shares in RAET in December.
Turnover in Getronics' software development and management operations grew by more than 25 percent in the first half, with project returns and fees also on the increase, the company said.

The group also won a large number of contracts for computer and network management during the period, and further consolidated its leading position in the area of personnel information systems, it said.

The financial position continued to improve, the company said, with the solvency ratio after correction for cash increasing to over 48 percent and shareholders' equity growing to 335 million guilders, up 29 percent from the end of 1996.
The group net margin rose to 6.2 percent from 5.1 percent in 1996, Getronics said. ($ = 2.063 Dutch Guilders)
